summary: The actor-independent direct skill-assignment store (cinatra#2346 S1, epic #2345). ONE new table agent_assigned_skills(agent_package_name text NOT NULL, skill_id text NOT NULL, "position" integer NOT NULL, created_by text NOT NULL, created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()) with PRIMARY KEY (agent_package_name, skill_id), a UNIQUE index on (agent_package_name, "position") and a lookup index on (skill_id). An admin pins up to three installed skill extensions to an agent extension from its settings page; the resulting rows must reach EVERY run of that agent, including background runs with no user attached, which is precisely what the existing owner-scoped custom_skill_assignments table cannot do (its read is actor-gated by principal/team/project/org, so an actor-less worker run resolves none of its rows). The row therefore carries NO owner tuple at all and is keyed by the CANONICAL agent package name, never a slug and never a template id, so a multi-template agent package shares one assignment set. The UNIQUE (agent_package_name, "position") index backs the atomic three-assignment cap: the write path serializes on the owning skill extension's lifecycle lock and then a per-agent advisory transaction lock before counting, computing the next position and inserting, and the unique index is the database-level backstop that stops two racing inserts that computed the same next position from both landing. created_by is NOT NULL because the surface records who assigned; it is deliberately NOT an audit-retention surface (the rows are configuration, and a completed extension uninstall deletes them). "position" is quoted at every use site because Postgres will shadow the bare identifier with the position() function in some grammatical positions. Additive and non-destructive: creates one new table and touches no existing row or column. Idempotent CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS / CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS twin of the fresh-install bootstrap DDL in agentAssignedSkillsSchemaQueries (src/lib/agent-assigned-skills-schema.ts, spread into buildCreateStoreSchemaQueries), shipped in the SAME PR (core__0085 / core__0086 precedent) and pinned by a DDL-parity test plus a real-Postgres two-arm test that proves the fresh-install bootstrap and the operator-upgrade migration converge on the same table. down() drops the table, reverting the instance to "no agent has a directly assigned skill"; automatic matching is untouched. SEQ IS PROVISIONAL: assigned at merge — shipped max on origin/main at build time is core__0088; a concurrent lane may claim 0089 first, in which case renumber-at-merge is normal. migrations/** is HIGH-RISK: owner approval required; the lane never merges.
